question: Under the CRR, when is an obligor considered to be in default?
expected_answer: When either or both apply: (a) the institution considers the obligor unlikely to pay its credit obligations in full without recourse to actions such as realising security; (b) the obligor is more than 90 days past due on any material credit obligation to the institution, its parent or subsidiaries.
author: claude-draft
notes: Wording checked in consolidated text (2026-06-26 version).

question: Can a bank apply the definition of default at facility level instead of obligor level, and for which exposures?
expected_answer: Yes, but only for retail exposures: institutions may apply points (a) and (b) of Art. 178(1) at the level of an individual credit facility rather than the total obligations of a borrower.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text. Alternatives accepted 2026-10-27 (retrieval review).

question: What are the maximum absolute and relative components of the materiality threshold for retail past-due credit obligations?
expected_answer: The authority-set absolute component must not exceed EUR 100 (or its national-currency equivalent). The relative component is between 0% and 2.5%, normally 1% where the authority considers that reasonable. Its denominator is the institution's, parent's and subsidiaries' total on-balance-sheet exposures to the obligor, excluding equity exposures. Both components must be exceeded for the material past-due criterion; the applicable consecutive-day period must also be met.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The non-retail EUR 500 cap is optional context, not a required fact for this retail question. These are RTS settings/caps, not an assertion of the actual setting in every jurisdiction.

question: What is the minimum probation period before a defaulted exposure (not under distressed restructuring) can be reclassified as non-defaulted?
expected_answer: At least three months after the conditions in CRR Articles 178(1)(b) and 178(3) cease to be met. This is a minimum probation period, not automatic cure; the other reclassification conditions must also be satisfied.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Alternatives accepted 2026-10-27 (retrieval review). Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: the three-month minimum and its start. Details of the broader cure assessment are optional. ECB 170/172 are not standalone equivalents for the minimum-period fact.

question: How long is the probation period for a defaulted exposure subject to distressed restructuring?
expected_answer: At least 1 year from the latest of: (a) extending the restructuring measures, (b) the exposure being classified as defaulted, (c) the end of the grace period in the restructuring arrangements. Reclassification also requires, among others, a material payment during that period, no past-due amounts and no remaining concerns about full repayment.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Alternatives accepted 2026-10-27 (retrieval review). Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Keep the one-year latest-of start and the cure conditions distinct. ECB 170/172/173 do not individually replace both EBA paragraphs. This reference uses the registered 2016 guideline wording; the 2026 amendment changes the forbearance terminology without changing the one-year minimum.

question: What diminished financial obligation threshold should trigger default for a distressed restructuring?
expected_answer: Institutions set a threshold for the diminished financial obligation (DO = (NPV0 - NPV1)/NPV0, discounted at the original effective interest rate) that should not be higher than 1%; above it the exposure is considered defaulted.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: When does the sale of credit obligations at a loss indicate unlikeliness to pay?
expected_answer: When the credit-related economic loss on the sale (L = (E - P)/E) is material; institutions set the materiality threshold, which should not be higher than 5%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: What is the PD input floor for IRB corporate exposures under CRR3?
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: What PD input floors apply to retail exposures under CRR3?
expected_answer: 0.1% for QRRE revolvers and 0.05% for other retail exposures; the PD used is the higher of the grade/pool PD and the floor. PD of defaulted retail exposures is 100%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: What minimum length of historical observation period is required for PD estimation?
expected_answer: Normally at least five years for at least one data source, using a longer available period where relevant and a representative mix of good and bad years. At IRB implementation, the competent authority may permit relevant data covering two years, then an additional year each year until five years is covered. For non-retail exposures this exception is restricted to institutions without permission to use own LGD estimates or IRB-CCF; the retail implementation exception is also subject to authority permission.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The concluding subparagraphs supply the implementation exceptions. A categorical five-year-only answer is incomplete; the two-year exception is not unconditional or available to every non-retail A-IRB institution.

question: What LGD input floors apply to retail exposures under CRR3?
expected_answer: Unsecured: QRRE 50%, other retail 30%. Secured: retail secured by residential property 5%; other retail secured by financial collateral 0%, by receivables 10%, by residential or commercial immovable property 10%, by other physical collateral 15%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: Into which categories must deficiencies be classified when quantifying the margin of conservatism (MoC)?
expected_answer: Identified deficiencies are classified into two categories: Category A, identified data and methodological deficiencies; Category B, relevant changes to underwriting standards, risk appetite, collection and recovery policies and other sources of additional uncertainty. Category C, the general estimation error, is not a deficiency category but a separate component of the final MoC (the sum of the MoC for A, B and C).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Reference reworded 2026-10-29 after judge spot-check: A/B are deficiency categories (para. 36), C is a separate MoC component (para. 42).

question: How does the CRR define a 'large corporate'?
expected_answer: A corporate undertaking with consolidated annual sales of more than EUR 500 million, or belonging to a group whose total consolidated annual sales exceed EUR 500 million.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text.

question: Under the ordinary CRR3 Article 125(1) loan-splitting treatment for an eligible residential-property exposure, with a sole first lien and no national override, what risk weight applies to the part up to 55% of the property value?
expected_answer: 20%. The question assumes eligibility for Article 125(1), a sole first lien and no higher national risk weight or lower national property-value percentage.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in text. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: 20% for the specified eligible part. Junior/pari-passu lien allocation and other property-treatment branches are optional context, not required facts.

question: What output floor factor may institutions apply in 2026 under the transitional arrangements?
expected_answer: 55% for the period from 1 January to 31 December 2026, under CRR Article 465(1)(b).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: the 2026 factor. Other phase-in years, the 72.5% end state and the conditional group/solo derogation are optional, not required to receive full answer credit.

question: An A-IRB bank has an exposure classified as general corporate, not specialised lending, to a non-financial corporate group with EUR 800 million consolidated sales measured under CRR Article 142(1)(5a). May it use own LGD and CCF estimates for that exposure?
expected_answer: No. The obligor is a large corporate (sales > EUR 500m), and under CRR3 exposures to large corporates (not in the specialised lending class) must use the supervisory LGD values of Art. 161(1) and SA-CCFs, i.e. F-IRB treatment.
author: claude-draft
notes: Art. 151(8)(c) checked in text. Needs definition lookup + scope rule. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The scenario expressly excludes the specialised-lending exception and treats sales as the regulatory measure, not an arbitrary single-year number.

question: In a jurisdiction where the competent authority set the retail materiality threshold at EUR 100 and 1%, a retail obligor owes EUR 120 past due, which is 3% of its exposure, for 95 days, then pays it off. Is it in default, and when can it return to non-default?
expected_answer: Yes: both the absolute (EUR 120 > EUR 100) and relative (3% > 1%) components are exceeded and the obligation has been past due more than 90 days, so it is in default. After repayment it can return to non-default only after a probation period of at least 3 months, considering the obligor's behaviour and financial situation.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: What does the regulatory framework require for downturn LGD, and what applies if no downturn can be observed in the bank's data?
expected_answer: Article 181(1)(b) requires downturn-appropriate LGD when more conservative than the long-run average. Identify downturn periods using the relevant economic indicators and their most severe 12-month values; the duration is at least 12 months and may be longer. Where observed loss data cannot support calibration, first consider estimating the downturn impact using Section 6 of the EBA downturn guidelines. Only where neither observed-impact nor Section 6 calibration is possible may the paragraph-36 fallback be used: justify that inability to the competent authority, include a strictly positive Category A MoC for missing data, and ensure final downturn LGD including MoC is at least min(long-run average LGD + 15 percentage points, 105%). No observed impact, no relevant data, and inability to estimate impact are different cases.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Note: 105% bounds the floor (min of LRA+15pp and 105%). Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: the normal downturn rule, consideration of estimated-impact calibration before the final fallback, and the conditional fallback safeguards. Do not infer a flat 15-point add-on whenever a bank lacks observed downturn data.

question: A defaulted corporate loan is restructured with a 2% NPV loss. How should the bank classify it and when can it be cured?
expected_answer: A 2% NPV loss exceeds the maximum 1% diminished-financial-obligation threshold, so the restructuring is a distressed restructuring and the exposure is (or stays) defaulted. It can return to non-default only after at least 1 year from the latest of extending the restructuring measures, the default classification, or the end of any grace period, and only if the para. 73 conditions are met (e.g. a material payment, no past-due amounts, no concerns about full repayment).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27.

question: An A-IRB bank recognises eligible financial collateral that fully secures an other-retail exposure after the relevant volatility and currency adjustments. Which CRR dependence/currency requirements and LGD input floor apply?
expected_answer: Consider dependence between the obligor and the funded protection or provider, and address significant dependence conservatively (Article 181(1)(c)). Treat currency mismatches conservatively in LGD (Article 181(1)(d)). The fully eligible secured floor is 0%, compared with 30% for unsecured other-retail exposures (Article 164(4)); full coverage after the relevant adjustments is required under Article 164(4a). Partially secured exposures instead use a weighted floor.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Replaces the earlier guarantee question. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The question supplies full eligible adjusted coverage. Details of the partial-collateral formula are optional context.

question: For an IRB institution covered by the ECB reporting Decision referred to in the February 2019 validation-reporting instructions, what PD back-testing does CRR Article 185(b) require, and how are the results submitted under Section 2.2 of those instructions?
expected_answer: Regularly compare realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade and analyse deviations outside the expected range. Use historical data covering as long a period as possible, document methods/data, and update the analysis and documentation at least annually; analogous comparisons apply to own LGD/CCF estimates. Under Section 2.2 of the February 2019 instructions, institutions covered by the Decision submit validation-exercise results to the ECB using its templates when submitting their annual internal-validation report.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Source is the Feb 2019 version; answer should state the date. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The reporting obligation is limited to institutions covered by the referenced Decision. AUC is not established by Section 2.2 and is not a required scoring fact. The instruction version is explicitly historical.

question: Which input and output floors constrain an ordinary IRB retail residential-mortgage portfolio in 2026, assuming no eligible sovereign/central-bank guarantee under Article 159a and an institution subject to the output floor without the group/solo derogation?
expected_answer: Per exposure, the normal PD input floor is 0.05% for retail exposures other than QRRE revolvers and the residential-property LGD input floor is 5%. In 2026 the output-floor factor is 55%, applied to the institution's total risk exposure amount by comparison with its standardised total, not independently to this portfolio. Input floors and the institution-wide output floor are distinct constraints.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The question expressly excludes the Article 159a and group/solo exceptions. Details of SA mortgage treatment are optional, not needed to explain the different floor levels.

question: Which CRR3 provision changed the PD input floor for IRB corporate exposures, and to what value?
expected_answer: Article 1, point (86) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 replaced CRR Art. 160(1), setting a PD input floor of 0.05% for corporate exposures (and inserting a separate Art. 160(1a) for regional governments, local authorities and public sector entities).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Old CRR2 value not in corpus, so the question avoids it.

question: According to the June 2026 ECB guide's foreword, what changed in its CCF-estimation content compared with the preceding guide, and why?
expected_answer: All content on estimating conversion factors (CCF) was removed because the EBA was preparing guidelines on that topic.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in the release table. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: removal of all CCF-estimation content and the stated reason. Release numbers, dates from the release table and the 2025 release history are optional.

question: What do paragraphs 1-3 of the ECB guide's foreword establish about its legal force and purpose, and do those passages alone establish whether an NCA-supervised less significant institution must follow the guide?
expected_answer: They explain the ECB's understanding of the applicable rules and its approach to assessing internal-model permissions, and support consistency among supervisory teams. The guide does not replace or overrule EU or national law. Those passages alone do not establish an obligation for an NCA-supervised LSI to follow the guide; that requires further evidence about the applicable supervisory framework.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text and reviewed 2026-10-27. Reference reworded 2026-10-29: 'does not address / passages do not say' phrasing accepted. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: A bounded answer acknowledging that LSI applicability is not established by these passages is required. Do not require an unsupported categorical SI/LSI allocation or imply that EBA guidelines have identical legal force to regulations.

expected_answer: Abstain: market risk (FRTB) is outside the credit risk corpus.
author: claude-draft
